summary: Package ships OpenSSL-encrypted opaque blobs re-exported as strings with placeholder metadata
details: The package main re-exports from apps/docs/app/theta.ts, which readFileSyncs two shipped OpenSSL 'Salted__'-prefixed encrypted files (apps/docs/app/rsa.db and apps/docs/app/des.db) and exports their contents as `rsaKey` and `desKey` strings. Within this tarball there is no decoder, no network I/O, no exec/eval, and no install lifecycle script that consumes these blobs, so the encrypted payload is inert on install and import of this package alone. The package.json is a bare workspace stub with name 'thedata', no description, no repository, no author, and no homepage, while presenting itself under a generic 'Theta Data API' framing. The combination of opaque encrypted blobs shipped and re-exported as raw strings from a placeholder-metadata package is unusual and structurally consistent with staging for a separate consumer that would decrypt and execute the blobs, but no such consumer or decrypt/exec path is present in this artifact.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
